**Summary**

I researched Apple's most recent results and confirmed them against primary sources (Apple Newsroom and the FY2024 Form 10-K on SEC EDGAR), because one search snippet contained wrong figures — a mirror-site listing claimed $361.2B revenue and $5.12 EPS, which the 10-K itself contradicts. The verified numbers show Apple's fiscal 2024 (ended Sept 28, 2024) total net sales of $391.0B, operating income of $123.2B, net income of $93.7B, and diluted EPS of $6.08 — with net income down year over year largely due to a one-time $10.2B income tax charge. The September quarter was solid, with revenue of $94.9B up 6% year over year, suggesting the iPhone 16 cycle and services growth were offsetting softness elsewhere; the tone of coverage around iPhone 16 demand and the Apple Intelligence rollout was cautious but stable rather than negative. Given continued revenue growth, very high operating margins (~31.5%), and no company-specific red flags, I judged AAPL a reasonable buy within your mandate. With the stock quoted at $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72), I placed a single limit buy order for 44 shares at $222.90 — just above the ask to favor execution while staying within pennies of the market — for a total of about $9,808, under the $10,000 per-order cap and well within the $20,000 daily limit. The order filled at $222.90. I did not touch MSFT (100 shares held) and made no fund transfers or withdrawals.
